hits.description:
Search Stellar docs about official developer tools and SDKs: the client SDKs list (JavaScript/TypeScript stellar-sdk npm package, Python, and the other language SDKs — which SDK to install for building Stellar and Soroban apps), the Stellar CLI (stellar contract deploy / invoke cookbook, key management, network configuration — the command sequence from new contract project to deployed contract), Stellar Lab (build, sign, simulate and submit transactions in the browser; API explorer for RPC methods and Horizon endpoints; view and decode XDR), the Quickstart docker image (run a full local Stellar network for development and CI), scaffold-stellar, OpenZeppelin contracts and relayer, ramps and infrastructure tools. Covers /docs/tools.

Returns: Array of tools/SDK hits: { url, url_without_anchor, anchor, breadcrumb, type, snippet }.

Tokenized real-world assets verified on Stellar. Every tokenized real-world asset rwa.xyz lists on Stellar (97 tokens, 52 issuers), each re-verified on-chain: classic assets from the issuer's own stellar.toml plus Horizon where the toml declares them (else on-chain-only), Soroban tokens from the contract's own metadata via RPC. state is live | issued-single-holder | deployed-no-supply | not-found; rows carry verificationLevel, evidenceUrl, verifiedAt, and pairedWith for a tranche deployed twice. Includes the fiat stablecoins rwa.xyz classes as RWA (productKind=stablecoin). Curated registry: absence means untracked, never 'not on Stellar'.

Search Stellar projects — look up a project by name, or find prior art / competitors. Search the curated directory of Stellar projects/products — what has been BUILT, by whom, with SCF funding, lifecycle status, builtBy, links, indexed repos, and verified on-chain metrics (onchain) inline. THE way to LOOK UP a specific project by its name (a named protocol/app/wallet/tool) AND to discover 'who/what already exists for X'; the type filter gives exact product-type rosters (Wallet, DEX, Oracle, Lending, Payments, Stablecoin, RWA…). Not for docs, standards, or how-to/reference knowledge → use searchResearch.

Catalog note: results are structured directory facts, not editorial pieces — for articles, AV, interviews, or research summaries about a project, use the lumenloop semantic and directory ops.

Search what was BUILT at Stellar hackathons (prior-art over prototypes). Topic search across every submission ('buidl') from all Stellar hackathons (DoraHacks) — the PROTOTYPE layer of prior art, most of which never becomes a directory project. Answers 'has anyone already built X at a hackathon?' with each build's name, description, event, placement/award, votes, and repo/demo links. winnersOnly=1 = prize winners; track filters by track. Absence is a real whitespace signal, not proof it was never tried. For SHIPPED products in the directory → use searchProjects.

Search all content semantically. Embeds the query text and finds similar articles, AV, events, and tweets via pgvector cosine distance. Use this (not search_documents/list_documents) whenever the query is conceptual or phrased as a question, or when you do not know which collection holds the answer; reserve search_documents for exact title/URL keyword lookup. Supports date/source/type filters — use these for scoped research queries like "find Stellar DeFi content from March" or "what did SDF post about privacy".

When to use: Meaning-based search across ALL published content types at once (articles, AV, events, research) — the default discovery tool for "what has been said about X". For exact-term lookup in one collection use search_documents; for content about one specific project use find_content_about_project. For "latest/current" ecosystem facts (protocol version, program/fund status, recent incidents or launches) prefer this over live web — results are dated and the corpus updates continuously; cite the date. Use web only for facts the corpus cannot hold, e.g. upstream package/registry pins (crates.io, npm, GitHub release tags).

Returns: Results grouped by content type, each with AI summary, source url, date, and similarity score — never full text. Cite the returned url. response_format 'concise' (external default) omits long_summary; pass 'detailed' to include it.

Catalog note: this is the wide-net recovery lane for open-world identity, history, event, and obscure-topic questions after directory, entity, or docs lookups are empty or off-target. Not for products/companies and their funding/status → use searchProjects.

Catalog note: repoScore, stars, rank, and directory presence are discovery metadata, not API, security, license, audit, maintenance, or production evidence. Verify those claims at the repository and primary sources before reusing code.

Search all content semantically. Embeds the query text and finds similar articles, AV, events, and tweets via pgvector cosine distance. Use this (not search_documents/list_documents) whenever the query is conceptual or phrased as a question, or when you do not know which collection holds the answer; reserve search_documents for exact title/URL keyword lookup. Supports date/source/type filters — use these for scoped research queries like "find Stellar DeFi content from March" or "what did SDF post about privacy".

When to use: Meaning-based search across ALL published content types at once (articles, AV, events, research) — the default discovery tool for "what has been said about X". For exact-term lookup in one collection use search_documents; for content about one specific project use find_content_about_project. For "latest/current" ecosystem facts (protocol version, program/fund status, recent incidents or launches) prefer this over live web — results are dated and the corpus updates continuously; cite the date. Use web only for facts the corpus cannot hold, e.g. upstream package/registry pins (crates.io, npm, GitHub release tags).

Returns: Results grouped by content type, each with AI summary, source url, date, and similarity score — never full text. Cite the returned url. response_format 'concise' (external default) omits long_summary; pass 'detailed' to include it.

Catalog note: this is the wide-net recovery lane for open-world identity, history, event, and obscure-topic questions after directory, entity, or docs lookups are empty or off-target. Raven normalizes every returned collection into one items array, globally sorted by the upstream similarity score; each row carries collection, while counts and meta preserve shape context. Filter items before projecting compact fields. Semantic rows are candidates, not attribution: require exact identity plus source and date, and discard merely adjacent results.

Map a sector or topic of the Stellar ecosystem into a landscape of projects, categories, regions, and related content using the LumenLoop directory and semantic search. Use when the user asks to survey, map, or get an overview of an area of Stellar (e.g. 'what RWA projects exist', 'map Stellar DeFi', 'who is building wallets').

Tokenized real-world assets verified on Stellar. Every tokenized real-world asset rwa.xyz lists on Stellar (97 tokens, 52 issuers), each re-verified on-chain: classic assets from the issuer's own stellar.toml plus Horizon where the toml declares them (else on-chain-only), Soroban tokens from the contract's own metadata via RPC. state is live | issued-single-holder | deployed-no-supply | not-found; rows carry verificationLevel, evidenceUrl, verifiedAt, and pairedWith for a tranche deployed twice. Upgrade Stellar/Soroban smart contracts using OpenZeppelin's upgradeable module. Use when users need to: (1) make Soroban contracts upgradeable via native WASM replacement, (2) use Upgradeable or UpgradeableMigratable derive macros, (3) implement atomic upgrade-and-migrate patterns with an Upgrader contract, (4) ensure storage key compatibility across upgrades, or (5) test upgrade paths for Soroban contracts.

Stellar smart contract development (Rust, soroban-sdk). Entry point with project setup, contract anatomy, and build/deploy workflow, routing to three companion files in this directory — development.md (storage/TTL, authorization, cross-contract calls, tokens, events, errors, upgrades, fees, troubleshooting), testing.md (unit, fuzz, property, fork, mutation, integration), and security.md (vulnerability classes, checklists, tooling, audits). Use when writing, testing, reviewing, securing, debugging, or shipping Stellar smart contracts, including anything the user calls "Soroban" — Soroban contracts, soroban-sdk, Soroban auth/storage/TTL errors, SEP-41 tokens, or SAC integration from contract code.

Keyword search restricted to ONE top-level category of the Stellar developer docs. Categories: build (smart contracts, guides, apps/dapps, security, agentic payments), data (Stellar RPC, Horizon, Hubble analytics, indexers/Galexie, oracles), tools (Stellar CLI, Lab, Quickstart, SDKs, developer tools), learn (protocol fundamentals: ledgers, accounts, transactions, operations, fees, consensus, lumens XLM, anchors, SEPs, migrate from EVM), platforms (Anchor Platform, Stellar Disbursement Platform), validators (running a stellar-core validator node), tokens (issuing assets, asset anatomy, access control, Stellar Asset Contract, token interface), networks (resource limits and fees), and meetings (protocol and developer meeting notes).
